decisions.quote:
Results: Within the population who grew up in the Soviet Union the coefficient of westward migration on Communist votes is -0.3483494 and larger in older group (-0.4511474) than in the younger group (-0.3483494). This claim was replicated. 
Deviations from the preregistration: none
Discussion: [optional]
Trace number: 14 / Claim ID: 2npy15
Coded claim 4 text (original paper): “Table 4 examines other dimensions of effect heterogeneity…The effect of westward migration on Communist votes is larger in older and less educated communities (columns 2–5 of Table 4). Overall, we observe that the effect is strongest for populations that were least likely to have been exposed to information and norms from the West. [Table 4, Prevalence of emigration to the West (percent), (4) = -0.66, standard error = 0.19; (5) = -0.41, standard error = 0.25]”
Replication outcome: Complex test
Inferential criteria: Within the population with higher education the coefficient of westward migration on Communist votes will be negative and larger in less educated group (below median) than in the more educated group (above median).
Results: Within the population with higher education the coefficient of westward migration on Communist votes is -0.56650702 but not larger in less educated group (-0.56650702) than in the more educated group (-0.2428117). This claim was not replicated.
decisions.reason: The report evaluates nine claims from Barsbai et al. (2017) with no single overall verdict; seven claims are explicitly reported as not replicated (including Claim 3n2npq quoted in the shipped row) while two claims (Claims 1r9r3o and y549wp) are explicitly reported as replicated, yielding a mixed outcome.
